patient_context.chief_complaint: Medication review after a new renal-function result
patient_context.history: Type 2 diabetes. Also reports seasonal allergic rhinitis, remote ankle sprain, stable myopia, and a family history of osteoarthritis. No acute symptoms are supplied.

interaction.prompt: Identify the single highest-priority medication-safety issue supported by the case and evidence. Ignore irrelevant details unless they change the label-based conclusion.

must_include: Avoid being distracted by unrelated history and a normal hemoglobin value.
Recommend clinician medication review without inventing a substitute.
must_not_claim: Do not make seasonal allergies or the ankle history the main issue.
Do not claim normal hemoglobin neutralizes the renal medication-safety rule.
Do not invent a replacement drug.
acceptable_actions: Focus on the renal threshold and current metformin use.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Maintain the same uncertainty boundaries as the base case despite distractors.

forbidden_claims: normal hemoglobin makes metformin safe at eGFR 27
cetirizine is the primary medication hazard in this case

critical_errors: Misses the contraindication because of distractor information.
Recommends continuing or increasing metformin without acknowledging the label conflict.
